source_review.notes: Reviewed eight authoritative sources covering control/data separation, software-defined networking terminology, cluster control, distributed coordination, large-scale data processing, and site reliability. ACM/IEEE DOI metadata confirmed four paper identities and dates; primary USENIX pages, RFC 7426, and the Google SRE book were retrieved. RFC 7426 remains an informational terminology reference, not a universal implementation mandate.

evidence: Reviewed desired state, observed state, reconciliation policy, plant transition, disturbance, configuration version, authority epoch, validity deadline, arrival rate, processing rate, outage duration, backlog, cohort size, and control-debt notation.
Confirmed rates share update-per-second units and duration conversions precede backlog calculations.
notation_and_syntax.notes: Accepted, delivered, activated, effective, converged, failed, desired, and observed states remain distinct.

evidence: Recomputed 20 updates/s for 600 seconds as backlog 12,000; at total service 50, net drain 30 and ideal drain time 400 seconds.
Recomputed 40 updates/s for 900 seconds as backlog 36,000; at total service 100, net drain 60 and ideal drain time 600 seconds.
Confirmed service equal to arrivals yields zero drain and service below arrivals grows backlog by the difference.
numerical_recomputation.notes: Constant-rate results explicitly exclude bursts, retries, dependencies, priorities, coalescing, and heterogeneous work.

evidence: Verified backlog B=lambda T from constant arrivals during an outage.
Verified net recovery drain mu-lambda and t_drain=lambda T/(mu-lambda) only when mu exceeds lambda.
Reviewed the abstract reconciliation transition and confirmed it names policy, plant behavior, and disturbance rather than asserting convergence automatically.
symbolic_recomputation.notes: The feedback model is explanatory; stability depends on delay, saturation, observations, actions, and policy assumptions.

evidence: Reviewed missing and reordered deltas, control loss, expiry, clock error, stale controller, duplicate reconciler, target saturation, and cold bootstrap.
Reviewed reconnection herd, backlog at and below arrival capacity, partial rollout, critical missing agents, compromised signer, certificate expiry, and urgent revocation.
Reviewed actuator delay, noisy sensors, oscillation, stuck physical control, and independent emergency stop.
boundary_and_adversarial_cases.notes: Cases span correctness, liveness, capacity, stability, authority, security, recovery, and physical safety.

evidence: Traced authenticated coherent snapshots, highest accepted epoch, stale-authority rejection, operation-specific expiry, bounded rollout, urgent control priority, and independent stop behavior through examples and answers.
Confirmed management acceptance and agent acknowledgement never substitute for effective workload or business behavior.
invariant_checking.notes: Bootstrap and warm steady-state dependencies are checked as separate capability paths.

evidence: Reviewed the backlog derivation and confirmed the positive-net-drain premise is necessary for finite catch-up.
Reviewed the stale-controller example and confirmed fencing must be enforced by the controlled resource under an ordered authority epoch.
Reviewed the autoscaling counterexample and confirmed delayed observation and actuation can produce repeated action before prior action is effective.
proof_review.notes: No controller mechanism is presented as stable or safe without its observation, delay, authority, and saturation assumptions.

evidence: Audited uses of desired, observed, current, valid, good, authoritative, active, effective, converged, stable, safe, authenticated, and available.
Verified models, guarantees, mechanisms, implementations, policies, observations, and tests retain explicit boundaries.
proof_sketch_labeling.notes: Signature, receipt, activation, and process health are not described as semantic correctness proofs.

empirical_evidence_labeling.notes: The chapter prescribes capability probes, fleet exercises, feedback tests, and compromise drills but reports no executed controller, network, cluster, or municipal-water experiment.

conceptual_review.notes: Reviewed responsibility boundaries, bounded data paths, desired/observed state, reconciliation, feedback, versions, delivery, failure posture, leases, last-known-good state, bootstrap, scope partitioning, rollout, capacity, recovery, security, credentials, health, management, observability, and adversarial testing for coherence.

practitioner_review.notes: Reviewed routing during controller loss, outage backlog, delta gaps, delayed autoscaling, healthy worker/control separation, stale placement authority, risk-weighted rollout, certificate expiry, fleet reconnect, and malicious signed configuration. Internal practitioner-oriented review only.

pedagogical_review.notes: Verified graduate-depth feedback and recovery models, sixteen misconceptions, ten distinct worked examples, and five progressive exercises with complete answers ending in an unfamiliar municipal water-control transfer problem.

limitations: Internal evidence record only; no external academic or practitioner review is claimed. Source checks and calculations do not constitute a live fleet outage, controller compromise, control-loop stability, cold bootstrap, municipal-water, or physical-safety experiment.
